title: A merge conflict between attempts dispatches a resolve-conflict job instead of stopping the run
description:
Observed 2026-09-23 on epic-yoh: cr4 and 7eq (same wave) both rewrote supervisePass in cloudflare/src/run-workflow.ts. cr4's attempt then failed to merge onto epic/yoh (merge_failed), and the run STOPPED for a person with lkd, ppt and gbs still running. The same shape stopped epic-wne twice (0ju/mrn add/add). The factory runs unattended; a stop whose only remedy is a person hand-merging two agents' work is a design defect (memory: factory-runs-unattended).

DO: on merge_failed for a content or add/add conflict between an attempt and the epic branch, dispatch a resolve-conflict job (the role already exists in the job contract, Phase 2) on a fresh worktree of the epic branch with the attempt's head merged in, conflict markers present, and both ticks' descriptions in the prompt. Its result is a merge commit whose parents are the epic head and the attempt head; the reconciler then treats the attempt as integrated (head contained) and runs the gate as usual. Route the job at the policy's ceiling tier (locally that is claude; in the cloud pi/GLM - never claude). A resolve job that fails, or a second conflict on the same tick, is the stop, as today.

Also: the planner should see this coming. Two same-wave ticks whose descriptions name one file (as cr4 and 7eq both named run-workflow.ts supervisePass) is a planning defect ky5's add/add note already calls out; a planning check that refuses same-wave ticks declaring the same file is the cheaper fix, and belongs with it.
notes:
2026-09-25 20:39 - ticfac run epic-gvc: 2p6 try 1 (run dispatch #1) reported a finding drafted for triage — proposed-tick "git log --full-history is required to read a merge commit against its path" (key daf02ac71924190018656adcb05ebabd6e1cabf948463ce7767d472760383df0, severity low, for this repository). Triage with `ticfac finding gvc daf02ac71924190018656adcb05ebabd6e1cabf948463ce7767d472760383df0 --promote-as <tick> --by "<who>"`, `--discard --by "<who>"`, or — when it was repaired inside this epic — `--fixed-as <commit> --by "<who>"`; the tick closes and the finding rides to the close-out, which does not hand over while it is untriaged.
2026-09-25 20:55 - ticfac run epic-gvc: 2p6 try 1 (run dispatch #1) merged into epic/gvc as 76abdf32ae12; the integrated gate (go, ts) passed.
acceptance_criteria: A run whose attempt conflicts with the epic branch dispatches a resolve-conflict job, integrates its merge, gates it and continues without a person; the job routes at the ceiling tier and never to claude in the cloud; a failed resolve is still a stop naming the files; a test drives a real content conflict through to integration
